packets.title: execution-core: write the four park markers on run_parkable round folds and stop a parkable loop at its first stale/closed fold save
packets.brief:
Context: session-core's crash park (WS03-S8, switch SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED, default off) re-seals a dead loop's last ROUND fold as a park and refuses any fold that lacks the route markers: session-core/src/loop_checkpoint.rs:793-799 returns `route_unrecorded` when `route_model_in`, `route_connection_in` or `child_ceiling_in` (non-zero) is missing, and crash_park_fold (loop_checkpoint.rs:814-828) takes the next park number from `parks_in(fold)`.

Defect 1 (D1-543/D1-549): execution-core writes the four markers (lf::EXT_PARKS, EXT_ROUTE_MODEL, EXT_ROUTE_CONNECTION, EXT_CHILD_CEILING) only in `park::park_fold` (runtime_loop/park.rs:368-395, doc comment says 'written here and nowhere else'). The round fold built at runtime_loop/agent.rs ~4348-4369 (`fold::build_fold(...)` then `folds.save_round(fold)`) carries none, so with the crash-park switch on every crash park is refused as route_unrecorded. Fix: when (and only when) the loop's `park_gate.run_parkable` is true (agent.rs ~2648, ParkGate), add the four markers to the round fold before `save_round`: EXT_PARKS = park_gate.parks_so_far (the resumed run's count from the claimed fold, so the park cap holds across crash resumes; a fresh loop writes 0), EXT_ROUTE_MODEL = ctx.route.model(), EXT_ROUTE_CONNECTION = ctx.route.subscription_connection_id(), EXT_CHILD_CEILING = the same child ceiling value the park site (ParkSite.child_ceiling) uses. Factor one helper in park.rs (e.g. `insert_route_markers(fold: &mut LoopFoldV1, site/route values, parks: u32)`) and make park_fold use it too, so both folds write identical keys; update the park.rs doc comment. Never write the markers on a non-parkable run: run_parkable already excludes approval continuations (holds_release), client/MCP-tool runs (tools_derivable false), ZDR, waived, Space, non-root and unpinned runs - reuse that one decision, do not add a second. Never write them on pre_effect, pause, fence or tombstone folds. Never copy session-core's `thread_watermark` extension into any executor-written fold (build_fold must keep starting from a fresh extensions map; session-core stamps round folds itself).

Defect 2 (D1-544, zombie loop): FoldWriter::apply (runtime_loop/fold.rs:1034-1051) marks the writer Failed on SaveError::Stale/Closed, and the loop only holds effectful calls afterwards (agent.rs ~3654-3672); it keeps running read-only rounds and can append a final answer. When session-core crash parks a loop that was merely slow, the live loop's next save goes stale and a continuation can run beside it, so two loops answer one run. Fix: for a run_parkable loop only, when a round/pre-effect save returns Stale or Closed (expose a narrow accessor on FoldWriter such as `lost_fence() -> bool` that is true only for State::Failed(SaveError::Stale|SaveError::Closed), not for Refused), stop the loop at that point before any further inference, append, receipt or tool dispatch, and end the RunAgent call with a typed status (e.g. Status::aborted("loop_checkpoint_superseded")) without reporting an answer. Check after save_round at the end of a round and wherever save_pre_effect returns Hold. Non-parkable runs must keep today's behaviour exactly (held effects, loop continues).

Must not change: behaviour with parking off or the crash-park switch off is byte-identical (markers only when run_parkable, which is false with parking off); no new switch; ZDR/waived runs never write folds; files are CRLF in this worktree - preserve line endings.

Tests to add (in the existing #[cfg(test)] modules using the session-core double already in agent.rs, which records loop_saves with their fold JSON): (a) a parkable run's round fold carries the four keys with parks=0 fresh and parks=N on a park resume seeded with N; (b) a non-parkable run (approval continuation / tools not derivable / parking off) round fold carries none of the four keys; (c) a park fold and a round fold of a run resumed from a session-core crash park (claimed fold containing extensions.thread_watermark) contain no thread_watermark key; (d) a parkable loop whose round save answers Status::aborted("loop_checkpoint_stale") (and failed_precondition loop_checkpoint_closed) makes no further infer call and reports no answer, while the same script on a non-parkable run keeps today's outcome; (e) a session-core-side-shaped check: the round fold JSON passes the same field rules as loop_checkpoint.rs:793-799 (non-empty route model/connection, child ceiling > 0).

packets.title: Two session-core DB tests fail on a real Postgres (harness 2026-10-26)
packets.brief:
# session-core DB harness, 2026-10-26 (full run, throwaway Postgres)

842 passed, 2 failed (exit 101). Last recorded full run before this: 719 passed (2026-10-22).
Every migration up to 0064 applied on a real Postgres in this run.

Failures (to fix, then re-run with the harness filters):
1. grpc::tests::record_scheduled_run_result_refuses_zdr_run (grpc.rs ~10908): the test marks a run zero-retention
   with an UPDATE after creating it, and the trigger refuses it: "run retention receipt is immutable". Test setup
   must create the run with its retention receipt from the start (or use the store's own creation path for a ZDR run).
2. memory_control::tests::pause_blocks_inline_and_dreaming_extraction (memory_control.rs ~1224): "the inline row
   appears while on" expected 1, got 2. Either the test counts rows another writer adds, or inline extraction writes
   twice while the user is on: investigate before changing the assertion.

Re-run: bash "apps/Model Plane/scripts/tests/session-core-db-tests.sh" record_scheduled_run_result_refuses_zdr_run=1 pause_blocks_inline_and_dreaming_extraction=1

Fix the first by creating the run with its zero-retention receipt from the start in the test setup (read how a ZDR run is created by the store and how the trigger guards the receipt; do not weaken the trigger). For the second, read memory_control.rs around line 1224 and the inline and Dreaming writers it exercises: decide from the code whether the second row is a legitimate row the test did not expect (fix the assertion and explain it in a comment) or a real double write (fix the writer). You cannot run the DB tests (no docker); make them compile and explain your reasoning; the lead runs them through the harness.

packets.title: Declare vision_as_parts and do_attachments in /v1/models and let the FE read them, plus compose pass-through
packets.brief:
The client gates image-as-parts and Do attachments on build-time VITE switches: attachment-policy.ts:41-53, visionAsPartsEnabled() reads VITE_CHAT_VISION_AS_PARTS_ENABLED and doAttachmentsEnabled() reads VITE_CHAT_DO_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED. These only mirror the server switches CHAT_VISION_AS_PARTS_ENABLED (vision_parts.rs:38) and CHAT_DO_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED (sse.rs:122), so the two sides can drift. The server-declared policy has only modes {vision, sandbox_files} (attachment_policy.rs:254-266 and 448-455). deploy/docker-compose.yml passes CHAT_VISION_AS_PARTS_ENABLED to model-gateway (line 319) but not CHAT_DO_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED.

Fix, server side:
- Add `vision_as_parts: bool` and `do_attachments: bool` to AttachmentModes. Fill them in AttachmentPolicy::from_getter from "CHAT_VISION_AS_PARTS_ENABLED" and "CHAT_DO_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED": only a trimmed literal `true` enables them, the same rule the existing switches use.
- Make vision_parts.rs's ENABLED_VAR pub and reuse it, rather than duplicating that literal.
- Add a pub const in attachment_policy.rs for the Do variable, with a comment that sse.rs's DO_ATTACHMENTS_VAR must equal it. Do NOT edit sse.rs, which belongs to another packet.
- Update the_declared_policy_is_the_documented_json (attachment_policy.rs:778) and tests/attachment_policy_contract.rs if it pins the modes shape.

Fix, client side:
- parseAttachmentPolicy (chat-client.ts:2979-3006) reads the two new fields as OPTIONAL booleans: absent means false, so an older server still parses. Expose them as modes.visionAsParts and modes.doAttachments.
- In attachment-policy.ts, visionAsPartsEnabled and doAttachmentsEnabled take the declared policy (or its modes) as an optional argument. They return the declared value when a policy is loaded and fall back to the VITE switch otherwise. Update their callers to pass the loaded declared policy (find them with grep).

Compose: add `CHAT_DO_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED: ${CHAT_DO_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED:-}` next to line 319 in the model-gateway service. Check whether the services at ~986 and ~1366 are model-gateway variants that also need it.

Must NOT change: both switches stay default off (empty or absent means off); with no policy loaded the FE behaves exactly as today; the five attachment codes are unchanged; sandbox_files keeps its meaning. Files are CRLF: preserve line endings.

Tests to add:
- Rust unit tests: the declared modes follow each env var, including that only the literal `true` enables them.
- Vitest in chat-client.attachment-policy.test.ts: the new fields are parsed, and a policy without them parses as false.
- A vitest showing that the gate functions prefer the declared policy over the VITE value.

packets.title: model-gateway serves POST /v1/models/access (label tiers mapped to the enum) and verdicts carry zdr_attested so the BFF ZDR write guard stops depending on the admin's own filtered catalogue
packets.brief:
The Verevon BFF ZDR write guard (`apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/orgs/model_entitlement.rs`, `zdr_write_refusal`, lines ~476-541) POSTs `{ "draft": <ModelPolicyDoc JSON>, "include_catalogue": true }` to model-gateway `POST /v1/models/access` and reads `catalogue[{id, entitled}]`. model-gateway has NO such route (only `.route("/v1/models", get(list_models))` at `apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/http_routes.rs:269`), so for every ZDR org with a restricting layer the guard gets a 404 and answers 503 `model_policy_guard_unavailable`: an admin can never save such a policy.

Part 1 (D1-491): add the route in http_routes.rs next to `/v1/models`, modelled on `list_models` (lines ~8882-8942: `Extension(Claims)`, `VerifiedInferenceBearer`, `authenticated_inference_request`). It calls inference-core `GetModelAccess` with the org id from the verified claims (never from the body), `include_catalogue` and `model`/`surface` from the body, and `draft` mapped from JSON to `ModelPolicyDoc`: `allow_mode`, `allow`, `deny`, `max_effort` as strings, `defaults` as `{surface: {model, effort}}` -> `SurfaceDefault` map, and `min_privacy_tier` given as org-core's lower-case LABEL (`""`, `global`, `eu_resident`, `zdr_contractual`, `sovereign`) mapped to the `PrivacyTier` enum (empty = UNSPECIFIED; an unknown label is a 400 typed error envelope, never silently UNSPECIFIED). Reject unknown top-level fields. Answer JSON: `state, enforced, revision, role, restricted, model_allowed, reason, default_model, default_effort, max_effort, min_privacy_tier` (as label, reuse `privacy_tier_label`), `can_manage`, and `catalogue: [{id, provider, entitled, reason, zdr_attested}]`. Errors: an entitlement `Refusal::from_status` -> `crate::model_access::http(&refusal)` (403/503 typed), PERMISSION_DENIED -> 403 typed envelope, anything else -> 502 typed envelope `{error:{code,message}}`; never echo the inference-core status message. Put the JSON<->proto mapping in `model_access.rs` as pure functions so it is unit-testable.

Part 2 (D1-490): the guard takes the attested set from `GET /v1/models` as the acting admin, which is filtered by that admin's own stored policy under enforce, so a model the admin cannot see but the draft would allow is not counted (refuses a legitimate ZDR policy). Add `bool zdr_attested = 5;` to `message ModelAccessEntry` in `apps/Model Plane/proto/model_plane/v1/inference.proto` (comment: whether the model's deployment carries a zero-retention attestation for chat; independent of the policy), fill it in inference-core `grpc.rs` `model_access_response` (around line 1401-1412) from the unfiltered `chat` list: true when the model's `features` contain `"zdr"` (pushed in `provider/mod.rs:~820`) or its `privacy_tier` is ZdrContractual or Sovereign (mirror `model_attests_zdr_for_chat` in the BFF `domains/orgs/settings.rs:36`). Regenerate the Go bindings with buf (`apps/Model Plane/go/gen/model_plane/v1/inference.pb.go`; do not touch the pre-existing local change in `go/gen/go.sum`). In the BFF guard, read attestation from the verdict's `zdr_attested` when every verdict carries it, and fall back to today's catalogue set only when the field is absent (older model-gateway); keep the fail-closed 503 for any unreadable answer. Update the `/v1/models/access` row in `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/endpoint-map.md` (it says 'until then').

Must NOT change: the BFF guard stays fail-closed; the route is unreachable for a non-manager (inference-core already refuses a draft/include_catalogue from a non-manager with PERMISSION_DENIED and with entitlement off answers `model_entitlement_unavailable` -> 503, keep both); `GET /v1/models` shape unchanged; nothing in the gateway decides entitlement itself; no content in logs; preserve each file's line endings. If adding the field changes the inference-core status golden, it should not (it is a response field) — if `the_committed_status_contract_is_what_the_code_produces` fails, stop and report.

Tests: model-gateway unit tests for the mapping (each tier label -> enum, empty -> UNSPECIFIED, unknown label -> 400, defaults map, unknown field refused) and a route test with a fake InferenceCore (the pattern in `http_routes.rs` tests around line 13448 `get_model_access`) asserting org id comes from claims, draft and include_catalogue are forwarded, the catalogue JSON carries `zdr_attested`, and a typed entitlement refusal maps to its 403/503; inference-core unit test in grpc.rs that `model_access_response` sets `zdr_attested` from features/tier on an unfiltered catalogue even when the draft refuses the model; BFF test in model_entitlement.rs: an attested model absent from the admin's filtered catalogue but `zdr_attested: true` and `entitled: true` in the verdicts lets the PUT through, and the existing guard tests stay green.

packets.title: Verevon v3: Model access settings tab reachable from the sidebar when the BFF switch is on; picker notice gets a class rule
packets.brief: The `/settings/model-access` route works by URL but no navigation shows it. (a) `apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/core/components/CoreSidebar.tsx:107` calls `applyDemoModeNavGate(sidebarSections)` with no options, and `applyDemoModeNavGate` (`src/features/core/lib/sidebar-navigation.ts:425-430`) hides item `settings-model-access` unless `options.modelAccessEnabled === true`. (b) The expanded settings panel (`src/features/core/components/sidebar/CoreSidebarSettingsPanels.tsx`, `settingsSidebarSections` lines 44-60) has no Model access link at all. Fix: read the BFF flag the same way `src/features/settings/components/OrgModelAccessSection.tsx:78-85` does: `createResource(() => (hasWorkspaceAdminAccess(session) && session.activeOrg?.id ? session.activeOrg.id : undefined), (id) => getModelEntitlement(id))` from `@/shared/api/model-entitlement-client`, with `enabled === true` as the flag; any error, a non-admin or a missing org means false (members get 403 from the BFF when the switch is on, so never fetch for them). Pass `{ modelAccessEnabled }` to `applyDemoModeNavGate` in CoreSidebar.tsx, and add a `{ id: 'model-access', label: 'Modelltilgang', icon: BrainCircuit, href: '/settings/model-access' }` entry to the settings panel shown only under the same flag (thread the flag in as a prop or share one small accessor; do not fetch twice per render; keep `getSettingsActiveSectionId` resolving `/settings/model-access` to `model-access`). (c) `src/shared/components/AiModelPicker.tsx:32-37,183` styles `.verevon-ai-model-picker__notice` with an inline `POLICY_NOTICE_STYLE`; move those four declarations into a `.verevon-ai-model-picker__notice` rule next to the other `.verevon-ai-model-picker` rules in `src/styles/global.css` and drop the inline style. Must NOT change: the tab stays hidden with the switch off (`{enabled:false}`), for non-admins, and on fetch failure; no build-time flag; demo-mode hidden ids unchanged. Tests: a vitest for the gate wiring (e.g. extend `CoreSidebar.home-tab.test.tsx` or a new `CoreSidebar.model-access.test.tsx`) mocking `getModelEntitlement` to `{enabled:true,...}` (link visible for an admin), `{enabled:false}` (hidden), rejected promise (hidden), and a member session (never called). The Playwright spec `tests/e2e/model-entitlement.spec.ts` needs a second Vite dev server and is a live proof, not part of this packet. Note: :5173 is a container that does not see host edits; verify with tests, not the running app.

packets.title: model-gateway: carry the composer's prompt tier plan into the inline chat tool rounds and answer call
packets.brief: WS02-S9 tiered Anthropic system blocks (inference-core switch INFERENCE_ANTHROPIC_TIERED_SYSTEM, default false) only reach the Do loop: execution-core sets InferRequest.prompt_tiers (runtime_loop/agent.rs:2407-2426, 2909). The inline chat path never sends one: sse.rs:2447 calls `prompt.render(cache_options.prompt_order())`, discarding the tiers, and tool_loop.rs:7202 hard-codes `prompt_tiers: None` in the decision-round InferRequest; the answer InferRequest at sse.rs:3051-3070 leaves it Default (None). Fix: (1) in sse.rs, when `cache_options.prompt_order()` is PromptOrder::StablePrefix use `prompt.render_tiered(order)` (prompt_context.rs:278) to get messages + `TieredPrompt::plan()` (mp_contracts::prompt_tier::PromptTierPlan {stable, context}); Legacy keeps `render` and no plan (byte-identical). Convert to `pb::PromptTierPlan { stable_messages, context_messages }` as Some only when stable+context > 0 and the turn is not ZDR (effective_zdr: keep a ZDR request unchanged). (2) Add a trailing parameter `prompt_tiers: Option<pb::PromptTierPlan>` to `run_tool_rounds_for_model` (tool_loop.rs:6751) and thread it through `run_tool_rounds_for_model_with_attachments` and the inner function to the decision InferRequest at ~7202. (3) Set it on the answer InferRequest at sse.rs:3051. (4) A plan is only true for the exact leading messages it was computed on: add one helper in prompt_context.rs, e.g. `fn plan_for(plan, composed: &[ChatMessage], outgoing: &[ChatMessage]) -> Option<pb::PromptTierPlan>` that returns the plan only if the first stable+context messages of `outgoing` equal those of the composed prompt (role and content) and are all role system; use it at both call sites (tool_decision_messages and retries/compaction may rewrite the list - when they do, send None). Must not change: legacy order output, any request when stable order is off, ZDR requests, the separate refusal boundary between gateway dispatch_tool and execution-core (do not touch dispatch logic). inference-core already validates the plan and ignores it with its switch off (provider/anthropic.rs:271-300). Tests: in prompt_context.rs tests - plan_for returns the plan for an unchanged prefix, None when a leading message changed, was removed, or a non-system message sits inside the counted range; in tool_loop.rs tests (existing inference double that records InferRequests) - the decision request carries the passed plan when the prefix is intact and None when the param is None; Legacy order yields None. Files may be CRLF in this worktree; preserve line endings.
